references.text: God commands the Israelites to build a sanctuary so that he may dwell among them, which parallels the promise of God's dwelling place among his people.
God promises to dwell among the children of Israel and be their God, a direct parallel to the promise of setting his dwelling among them.
Ezekiel prophesies about an eternal covenant of peace where God's dwelling will be with the people, and he will be their God.
The nations shall know that the Lord sanctifies Israel when his sanctuary is in their midst forever.
God declares this to be the place of his throne and the footstool of his feet, where he will dwell among the children of Israel forever.
The Word became flesh and took up residence (ἐσκήνωσεν) among us – a fulfillment of the promise of God's presence among his people.
Paul quotes the promise that God will dwell among his people and walk among them, referencing that believers are the temple of the living God.
The final fulfillment of the promise: God's dwelling is with humanity; he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people.
